title: MCP default tool set: policy group on by policy evidence, analysis group opt-in; hunch_context advertises a lean landscape schema
context: #368: hosts that load every tool schema paid ~81k chars (42 tools) per session. David asked for the best option for Hunch users (2026-09-24).
decision: Add MCP tool groups `policy` (7 hunch_policy_* tools, enabled by default when PolicyRepository lists any policy) and `analysis` (project DNA/match, change proof/identity, shortlist, evidence map, wiki status; opt-in via HUNCH_MCP_TOOLS or .hunch/config.json mcp_tools). Hidden tools are filtered at the registerTool wrapper. The grounding block names policy tools only when the repo holds a committed public policy (never env/gitignored config, so the committed block is machine-independent). hunch_context advertises landscape by identity fields + passthrough; the handler still parses with the full DELIVERY_OUTPUT_SCHEMA.
consequences: Default tools 42 -> 27; empty-store tools_list 75.6k -> 37.4k chars, core 43.5k -> 29.3k
hunch_change_proof/identity have no CLI twin: orchestrators must enable analysis (CHANGELOG at release)
Toolset resolved once per process; a re-homed server keeps it until restart
alternatives_rejected: Drop outputSchema on hunch_context entirely — tests pin it and validating hosts lose the contract
Four-tool default (orient/why/check/record) — breaks verdict and task loops the hooks and grounding rely on
Gate the grounding policy line on .hunch/config.json — it is gitignored, so the committed CLAUDE.md would differ by machine (critic finding)
